title: John Bolton Pleads Guilty to Illegally Retaining National Defense Information
detail: Former National Security Adviser John Bolton pleaded guilty on June 26, 2026 in the US District Court for the District of Maryland (Greenbelt) to one count of unauthorized retention of national defense information, resolving an 18-count indictment stemming from classified diary-style entries he shared with family members while preparing his memoir 'The Room Where It Happened.' The charge carries a maximum 10-year sentence, though the plea agreement recommends capping prison time at 5 years; Bolton also agreed to pay a $2.25 million fine (half within 5 days, remainder within 90 days), forfeit his federal retirement pay, complete up to 100 hours of community service, and submit to an intelligence debriefing. Sentencing is scheduled for October 28, 2026. Bolton, 77, became a prominent Trump critic after leaving the administration in 2019.

media.caption: John Bolton arrives at US District Court in Greenbelt, Maryland to plead guilty to retaining classified information

title: House Oversight Committee Subpoenas Billionaire Leon Black Over Epstein-Related NDAs
detail: The House Oversight Committee served billionaire investor Leon Black with subpoenas on June 26, 2026 after he refused, during a voluntary interview, to answer questions about non-disclosure agreements tied to his years-long financial relationship with Jeffrey Epstein. Committee Chair James Comer's subpoenas compel Black to sit for a videotaped deposition under oath, scheduled for July 16, 2026. The subpoena is part of the broader congressional Epstein-files probe operating under the Epstein Files Transparency Act.
